about.title: San Carlos Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Carlos sees a steady stream of crash reports each year, with public records showing 85 injury collisions and 109 people hurt in the most recent final year alone. Many of these happen along the city's busiest stretches — El Camino Real, US-101, San Carlos Avenue, and Holly Street — with reports tending to cluster on Friday evenings when commuter and local traffic overlap. Whether you were rear-ended near a Caltrain crossing, sideswiped merging onto the freeway, or hit at a signal downtown, the aftermath usually means medical appointments, insurance calls, and missed work all at once. We handle personal injury claims from San Carlos car accidents, evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and explain your options under California law. There's no cost for a free consultation, and we work on contingency, so you owe nothing unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why San Carlos Residents Choose Us

items.title: You Have a Limited Window to Act
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early helps preserve your options before deadlines quietly pass.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you're found partly at fault, though your share of responsibility reduces the amount. We can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you by the other side.

items.title: No Cap Means Full Value Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, so how your losses are documented and presented can matter a great deal. It's worth talking to us before accepting an early settlement offer.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since insurers often use those statements to minimize claims later. Anything you say can be replayed out of context, even if you were just being polite or unsure about details. We can advise you on what, if anything, to communicate directly.

items.question: What should I do right after a crash on a road like El Camino Real or Holly Street?
items.answer: If you're able, document the scene with photos, get contact information from witnesses, and seek medical care even if injuries seem minor at first. Evidence like skid marks, traffic camera footage, or damaged property tends to disappear quickly on busy San Carlos corridors. The sooner details are preserved, the stronger a potential claim tends to be.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a free case review?
items.answer: Nothing — we offer a free consultation, and there's no obligation to move forward after you contact us. We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. You won't pay out of pocket to explore your options.
